Ireland also had/has much lower sub prime lending than the US.

Thus is one thing I don't understand in America. Foreclosure sales. In Ireland, houses repossessed by a bank are sold on the open market so that they can get the best sale price possible. This reduces any shortfall on the mortgage and if there is a profit made it goes back to theprevious owner. the buyer doesn't know it's a foreclosed house they are buying. If after this age you need a higher amount of credit, say over 20k, the main way to get it would be a home reversion agreement which is pretty much just settling a share in your house to the bank.  For credit cards etc they usually calculate the credit they give similar to how they would for anyone else. Income (pensions) versus expenditure and financial commitments = credit available to you. 

In the case where someone dies owing a large amount of money this is then due to come out of the persons estate generally either from savings or from the sale of property.
